<a2ui>
surface("status-list")
filter = segmented_control([{label: "All", value: "all"}, {label: "Done", value: "done"}, {label: "In progress", value: "in_progress"}, {label: "Blocked", value: "blocked"}], "all", "status_filter")
items = entity_list([
  {name: "Migrate billing database", subtitle: "Cutover completed with zero downtime", status: "Done"},
  {name: "Redesign onboarding flow", subtitle: "Prototype is in user testing this week", status: "In progress"},
  {name: "Upgrade payment gateway SDK", subtitle: "Waiting on vendor to release the sandbox keys", status: "Blocked"},
  {name: "Publish API v2 docs", subtitle: "Live on the developer portal since Monday", status: "Done"},
  {name: "Set up regional failover", subtitle: "Terraform modules are 70% written", status: "In progress"},
  {name: "Security audit remediation", subtitle: "Legal review is pending on the data-retention clause", status: "Blocked"},
  {name: "Mobile push notifications", subtitle: "Beta rolled out to 10% of users", status: "In progress"},
  {name: "Retire legacy login page", subtitle: "Redirects deployed and old routes removed", status: "Done"}
])
root = columns(2, "1.5rem", "top", [
  {blocks: [heading("Project items"), body("Filter the eight items by status."), filter]},
  {blocks: [items]}
])
</a2ui>

The catalog has no way to bind the filter to the list, so the status control won't hide rows by itself. The host has to wire `status_filter` to the list for filtering to take effect.
